name: Rubrik
thesis: Cyber-resilience platform displacing legacy backup/recovery vendors (Cohesity, Veeam, legacy Dell PowerProtect) as enterprises consolidate ransomware recovery + cloud data protection onto a single subscription platform. The bet: (1) net new subscription ARR continues at $100M+ quarterly cadence, (2) NRR holds >120% as land-and-expand deepens within existing accounts, (3) operating leverage continues to inflect as the IPO-era customer-acquisition cost cycle normalizes (Q4 sub ARR contribution margin jumped from 2.1% to 11.6% YoY).
key_driver: Net new subscription ARR cadence + sub ARR contribution margin inflection

tier_1_kpis.name: Net new subscription ARR ($)
tier_1_kpis.break_condition: <$80M for 2 consecutive Qs (deceleration to pre-FY26 levels)

tier_1_kpis.name: Sub ARR contribution margin
tier_1_kpis.break_condition: Inflection reverses — margin contracts QoQ for 2 Qs without explicit go-to-market reinvestment rationale

tier_1_kpis.name: Customers >$100K ARR
tier_1_kpis.break_condition: <15% YoY (large-customer attach is the moat signal)

nuance.bear_case: A Cohesity/Veeam consolidation play (PE-backed merger creates a credible scaled competitor) could compress RBRK's pricing power before scale economics fully kick in. Backup/recovery is historically a price-competitive category once the differentiation cycle ends.
nuance.adversarial_take: 34% sub ARR growth at $1.5B base is excellent, but the law of large numbers will bend the trajectory by FY27. The thesis must accommodate growth deceleration to ~25% as the new normal without panicking — break threshold below 25% is calibrated for that.
nuance.stress_test: If $100K+ customer growth slows below 15% AND a competitor M&A creates a >$3B scaled rival, the moat thesis weakens even before any single break trips.

thesis_breakers_qualitative: Net new sub ARR <$80M for 2 consecutive Qs
Sub ARR contribution margin reverses inflection
Major competitor M&A creating scaled rival (Cohesity-Veeam-Druva combination, etc.)
